page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192 is a high-capacity server instance powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processors running at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It features 192 virtual CPUs mapped to 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 720 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 3.75 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and standard network interfaces. The processor architecture includes advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography features like AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark evaluations place this server in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests. Memory performance is highly competitive, with read-only and write-large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks consistently ranking in the top ten percent. The system excels in parallel processing tasks, achieving top-tier results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, software compilation with Clang, and ray tracing. It also demonstrates strong performance in database operations, handling Redis SET operations at 212.26 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 227.94 GB per second. For machine learning workloads, the hardware-assisted AMX instructions enable top-tier prompt processing speeds for large language models and strong text generation capabilities.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-standard-192 offers high resource density and compute power for enterprise-scale workloads without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing for precise scaling of network-attached volumes. This server is highly suited for compute-heavy and parallelized workloads, including large-scale software compilation, high-throughput web serving, database management, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
